notes: Works and is well tested (unit, handler and integration), but it is over-engineered: reverse-proxy knowledge lives in celmatcher, it adds literal-concat constant folding, an rp.* alias and a 'linter appeasing' switch, which expands scope beyond what was needed.

Works correctly and is slightly more precise because it folds literal concatenations, but it is heavier than needed: the response placeholder list sits in caddyhttp, it adds a recursive name resolver and an extra interface, and it adds a fixed-port integration test on top of the unit tests.

Essentially identical to the reference fix, plus a handler-level regression test covering request-only, upstream.host, escaped-literal and status_codes expressions; it lacks a positive ph() or dynamic-name test.

Matches the reference exactly: the generic Placeholders() accessor lives in caddyhttp, the response placeholder list lives in reverseproxy, dynamic names are flagged, and an end-to-end table test covers the request-only, upstream.host, escaped-literal and status_codes cases, though it adds no positive-case tests for direct ph() calls.

Correct AST-based detection with good tests, but it hardcodes reverse-proxy placeholder names inside caddyhttp's CEL matcher, adds an unneeded value-type switch case and speculative rp.* handling, which is a layering smell.

Correct AST-based detection with thorough unit and end-to-end tests, but it puts reverse_proxy-specific placeholder knowledge (and a never-reached rp. alias) inside the generic caddyhttp CEL matcher and adds a redundant value-type switch case.

Walks the checked AST at provision time to record literal placeholder names plus a dynamic flag, and keeps the response-placeholder list in reverseproxy; it closely mirrors the reference, with thorough unit and handler tests (the internal slice is returned uncloned, a minor nit).

A neat Placeholders()/dynamic accessor using ast.MatchDescendants with the classification kept in reverseproxy, well tested at both the CEL and the proxy level; the only nit is that it returns the internal slice without cloning it.

Clean generic ReferencesPlaceholder(predicate) API that treats dynamic names conservatively, with response knowledge kept in reverseproxy; tests cover comprehensions, escaped literals, near-miss names and an end-to-end no-retry case.

A clean generic ReferencesPlaceholder(predicate) API keeps response knowledge in reverseproxy and treats dynamic names conservatively; its table test covers ph() calls, mixed and nested expressions, near-miss names and literals, plus an end-to-end POST check.
